description: Family-level contamination and held-out protection registry for reviewed Pilot A/B records.

families.name: Communication, conflict, and boundaries
families.description: Ordinary conflict, healthy boundaries, recipient withdrawal, and interaction loops that remain distinct from safety risk.
families.protectionReason: Related communication patterns can leak whether conflict intensity is incorrectly treated as safety risk.
restrictions: Disclose cross-role communication siblings in evaluation reports.
Do not use held-out members for prompt or few-shot construction.

families.name: Distress, humor, and disappearance
families.description: Humorous, figurative, employment, social, emotional, and death-adjacent meanings of similar severe surface language.
families.protectionReason: The records form designed contrasts where humor and disappearance wording change meaning with context.
restrictions: Exclude held-out members and their scenario structure from training and calibration.
Exclude protected humor/disappearance templates from synthetic generation.
Report results by family rather than as independent samples.

families.name: Location sharing, control, and tracking
families.description: Consent, reassurance seeking, monitoring, punishment, autonomy restriction, and tracking across turns.
families.protectionReason: Single-turn and multi-turn records share a consent-to-control semantic ladder.
restrictions: Exclude held-out members from training, few-shot examples, calibration, and retrieval.
Protect the consent-to-punishment evidence sequence from synthetic templates.
Disclose sibling exposure when reporting held-out results.

families.name: Self-harm, retraction, and escalation
families.description: Indirect and direct self-harm language, retraction, minimization, and Level 4 to Level 5 transitions.
families.protectionReason: The records intentionally vary disclosure, retraction, masking, immediacy, and current action risk.
restrictions: Exclude held-out members from all training and development exposure before evaluation.
Do not use protected self-harm evidence sequences as generation templates.
Report retraction and escalation subgroups separately.

families.name: Violence and immediate danger
families.description: Future or conditional violence intent contrasted with current external danger and emergency language.
families.protectionReason: The small sample is useful for timing and severity regression but cannot support independent category statistics.
restrictions: Keep held-out immediate-danger transitions protected until evaluation is complete.
Do not infer production performance from this small family.

families.name: Quoted, fictional, and third-party threats
families.description: Severe threat wording attributed to games, fiction, history, or other speakers rather than the user.
families.protectionReason: These are scarce negative controls for attribution and figurative-language false positives.
restrictions: Protect held-out attributed-threat examples from prompt construction.
Retain the family as a regression and attribution-boundary test.
